note:
#4871's reported symptom is a wrong-code miscompile, not a crash or a missing diagnostic: `Func(--i)` -- an empty inout function called with a pre-decremented argument -- lowers the pre-decrement to a magnitude-2 subtraction instead of magnitude-1, i.e. the decrement is silently applied twice. There is no error or warning either way, so a diagnostic-text predicate cannot see this at all; the only observable is the literal constant operand of the generated `add` instruction.

Clause 1 (positive anchor): `define void @PSMain(` must appear in the disassembly. This proves the compile reached codegen and produced the entry function -- a rejected/failed compile emits neither this nor any `add i32` line, so it cannot satisfy clause 2 by accident. Anchoring on the general LLVM `%[\w.]+` SSA-name form (not a numeric `%N` or a fixed name like `%dec1`) rather than a specific register spelling, per SKILL.md's IR-portability guidance -- LLVM SSA numbering is not stable across dxc versions and older releases can print named values.

Clause 2 (the symptom): an `add i32 <reg>, -2` reaching an arithmetic op. Anchoring on the literal `-2` distinguishes the reported bug from *correct* behaviour, which is `add i32 <reg>, -1` for exactly the same source line -- see the plain-decrement and separate-decrement controls below, both of which emit `-1` and must NOT match this predicate.

CONTROLS (all captured as variant-*.txt, run with cmd.txt's exact stage/entry arguments):

  control-plain-decrement.hlsl (--expect no-match): `--i; return i;` with no inout call at all. Emits a single `add i32 %0, -1`. Proves the compiler's baseline pre-decrement lowering is correct and that a bare `-1` is visible to this reader -- i.e. the predicate can tell -1 from -2, it does not just always fire.

  control-separate-decrement.hlsl (--expect no-match): `--i;` as its own statement, THEN `Func(i)` with the already-decremented value. Also emits a single `add i32 %0, -1`. Isolates the defect to the *argument expression* itself: calling the inout function `Func` at all, with a value that happens to have been decremented earlier, does not doubly subtract. Only writing `--i` directly as the call's argument expression triggers the bug.

  control-no-decrement-call.hlsl (--expect no-match): `Func(i); return i;` -- no decrement anywhere in source. No `add i32` line at all, confirming clause 2 is not vacuously satisfied by the inout copy-in/copy-out machinery alone; the anti-vacuity control for a presence predicate.

LIMIT: this predicate is scoped to a single unsigned pre-decrement written as an inout call argument; it says nothing about post-decrement, increment, or other inout expression shapes, which were not probed.
